discovery: Conformal field theory in two dimensions and the exact theory of critical phenomena

nominees.name: Alexander A. Belavin
nominees.affiliation: Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russia

subfield: Theoretical physics: quantum field theory and statistical mechanics
motivation: In 1984 Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov showed that scale invariance at a critical point, extended to local conformal invariance, fixes two-dimensional critical systems completely. Using the infinite-dimensional Virasoro symmetry, their minimal models give exact critical exponents and correlation functions for the Ising, Potts and tricritical universality classes. This turned the renormalization-group picture of phase transitions into an exactly solvable theory. The framework now underlies string theory, the quantum Hall edge, Kondo physics, SLE in probability and holography. Polyakov's earlier insight that critical fluctuations are conformally invariant, and his conformal bootstrap programme, foreshadowed the modern numerical bootstrap, which now gives the best determinations of the three-dimensional Ising exponents. Zamolodchikov's c-theorem and his exact integrable S-matrices extended these results away from criticality. Simple symmetry principles here reveal deep hidden order in fluctuating matter, confirmed by experiment and by numerical simulation.
